title: Make stable shim linters reliable in partial clones
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack) (oldest at bottom):
* #191266
* __->__ #191364

We've tried a lot of partial fixes to this partial clone problem,  which then caused more holes that required patching. The latest was: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/191228 which attempted to enforce certain git commands be local only. This was too strict, where the historical versions of files would error (see https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/actions/runs/30380274127/job/90346227990).

Codex and I tried to solve this problem once and for all with a small redesign. We have separated out the git commands that should require network, and the ones that should not:

Must remain offline: refs + commits, which we should trust our checkout.
  - merge_base_with_main() `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git merge-base HEAD refs/remotes/origin/main`
  - Working-tree diff: `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git diff HEAD -- <file>`
  - First attempt of every historical object command.

May contact the network: actual file content.
  - Latter attempts of every historical object command, assuming the first local attempt failed:
```
git diff <merge-base>..HEAD -- <file>
git ls-tree -z <revision> -- <path>
git cat-file blob <oid>
```

Removed:
  - `git ls-remote`: trust the local main, do not refetch main.
  - Explicit `git fetch origin <object-oid>`: GitHub can reject this request if it's a blob vs a commit/branch. We replace this with cat-file.
  - Fetching or updating origin/main or any linter-managed ref updates: lint runs concurrently, don't step over each other's toes

I'm relatively confident about the must remain offline, because our checkout for lint does the following:
  - setup-linux defaults to checkout-mode: treeless.
  - checkout-pytorch defaults to fetch-depth: 0, meaning full commit history.
  - origin/main is fetched by checkout.
